boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named public destinations along the USD-area corridors toward Linda Vista, Old Town, and Mission Bay.

cards.title: Linda Vista Road: public study rooms
cards.subtitle: Linda Vista Road corridor
cards.notes: Bring a library card or ask staff about the branch’s public computers and meeting/study room before settling in.
cards.short_summary: A city library branch with public computers and a meeting/study room.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists 19 public-use computers and one meeting/study room at Linda Vista Library, which is on Linda Vista Road.
cards.access_notes: Check the City’s current branch hours before visiting.

cards.title: Presidio Drive: two miles of trails
cards.subtitle: Presidio Drive corridor
cards.notes: Follow the signed Old Presidio Historical Trail for a self-guided walk, and stay on established paths.
cards.short_summary: A historic hilltop park with trails and an interpretive walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says Presidio Park has more than two miles of trails and a signed, self-guided Old Presidio Historical Trail.
cards.access_notes: Use designated paths and observe posted park rules.

cards.entity_name: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park
cards.title: San Diego Avenue: restored historic buildings
cards.subtitle: San Diego Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Start at the visitor center, then use the park map to connect its historic buildings, outdoor exhibits, and programs.
cards.short_summary: A state historic park interpreting early San Diego through buildings and exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: California State Parks documents museum exhibitions, restored historic buildings, living-history demonstrations, and special events at the park.
cards.source_title: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park
cards.access_notes: The park lists visitor-center and select-museum hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; verify before travel.

cards.title: Taylor Street: a transit transfer point
cards.subtitle: Taylor Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the station’s posted maps and real-time tools to plan a rail or bus transfer rather than relying on memory.
cards.short_summary: An MTS station at 4009 Taylor Street.
cards.evidence_claim: MTS identifies Old Town Transit Center at 4009 Taylor Street and lists its hours as 6 a.m.–9 p.m.
cards.access_notes: MTS lists station hours as 6 a.m.–9 p.m.; confirm service and platform details before departing.

cards.title: West Mission Bay Drive: playground and water access
cards.subtitle: West Mission Bay Drive corridor
cards.notes: Use the marked facilities for a daytime shoreline stop; the City notes a playground, picnic tables, and water access.
cards.short_summary: A Mission Bay park site with recreation facilities and lifeguard coverage.
cards.evidence_claim: The City places Bonita Cove at 1100 West Mission Bay Drive and lists a playground, water access with lifeguard on duty, picnic tables, grills, and fire rings.
cards.access_notes: The City lists availability from 4 a.m.–10 p.m.; the parking lot closes at 10 p.m.

cards.title: West Vacation Road: model-boat watching
cards.subtitle: West Vacation Road corridor
cards.notes: Walk the pond edge and watch scheduled model sail or power-boat races from the adjacent shaded turf area.
cards.short_summary: A Mission Bay pond used for sail and power model-boat races and regattas.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says Model Yacht Pond is used for sail and power model boats in races and regattas and is reached via West Vacation Road.
cards.access_notes: The City lists the area as open 4 a.m.–2 a.m. and states alcohol is not permitted.

cards.entity_name: Rose Marie Starns South Shores Park
cards.title: Sea World Drive: boat-ramp access
cards.subtitle: Sea World Drive corridor
cards.notes: Use the small grassy area and picnic tables for a short waterside stop, keeping clear of the boat-ramp traffic.
cards.short_summary: A small Mission Bay park oriented around boating access.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes Rose Marie Starns South Shores Park as a small boating-focused park with a boat ramp, grassy area, picnic tables, and restrooms.
cards.access_notes: The City directs visitors from Sea World Drive and lists the park as open 4 a.m.–2 a.m.; alcohol is not permitted.

cards.title: East Mission Bay Drive: accessible playground
cards.subtitle: East Mission Bay Drive corridor
cards.notes: Use the playground, rinse-off shower, picnic tables, or jogging and bike path while observing posted shoreline conditions.
cards.short_summary: A Mission Bay shoreline site with play, picnic, and path amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists a playground, picnic tables, grills, fire rings, rinse-off shower, and jogging or bike path at Tecolote Shores North.
cards.access_notes: The City lists availability from 4 a.m.–2 a.m., notes no lifeguard is on duty, and prohibits alcohol.

cards.title: Fiesta Island Road: a park-island loop
cards.subtitle: Fiesta Island Road corridor
cards.notes: Follow the posted route from East Mission Bay Drive and use the island’s public roads and designated recreation areas.
cards.short_summary: A named Mission Bay park destination reached from East Mission Bay Drive.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s directions route visitors from Sea World Drive to East Mission Bay Drive and then left to Fiesta Island, with parking throughout the island.
cards.access_notes: Check City notices for events, permits, and any area-specific restrictions before visiting.

cards.title: Mariners Way: least-tern observation
cards.subtitle: Mariners Way corridor
cards.notes: Observe from outside fenced nesting areas and do not approach or disturb birds, especially during the breeding season.
cards.short_summary: A Mission Bay wildlife-tour stop associated with California least terns.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s self-guided wildlife tour identifies Mariner's Point as habitat for the federally listed endangered California least tern and advises that disturbance can cause nest abandonment.
cards.source_title: Self Guided Tour of Wildlife Preserves
cards.access_notes: Respect fences and signs protecting nesting habitat; the City notes June or July as the nesting period.
